parsed.corrected_rationale: The answer refers to "several recent efforts to study the problem of geographical adaptation" and mentions specific works [1,2,3] that are not cited or compared. It also points out that the conclusion about scaling model sizes and datasets not yielding geographical robustness is related to GeoNet. However, the comment never pinpoints a locatable part of the reviewed paper — it cites no section, table, figure, or unique passage, only a general conclusion from the missing related work GeoNet. The comment does clearly specify what needs to be addressed (a discussion of and comparison with GeoNet and the cited works), so the needed action is identifiable even though the referenced part of the paper is not. Because the authors cannot confidently determine which part of the paper the comment addresses, it does not meet the rubric criteria for a fully grounded comment; instead, it aligns with the mid-level rubric description where the referenced part cannot be confidently determined but the required action is clearly specified.
